target.title: feat(sakana): surface pay-as-you-go credit balance
target.body:
## Summary
- Sakana's existing provider (#1774) only reads the **Subscription** tab of `console.sakana.ai/billing` for the 5-hour/weekly quota windows. Fugu Ultra's pay-as-you-go credit balance and usage total live on the same page's **Pay as you go** tab, which the server only renders when the request includes `?tab=payAsYouGo` — so it's fetched as a second, best-effort GET alongside the existing subscription request, using the same cookie header.
- Adds `SakanaPayAsYouGoSnapshot` + a parser for the credit balance, rolling usage total, and date-range label, matching the tab's real rendered markup (including React's `<!-- -->` hydration-boundary comments between interpolated text nodes).
- The second request never throws: any failure (network error, non-200, wrong origin, unparseable markup) just omits the field, so an account without PAYG access still gets its quota windows exactly as before — verified with a dedicated test.
- Wires `supportsCredits: true` + a `Balance:`/`Recent usage:` menu row and menu bar text, mirroring the existing MiMo balance display pattern (`sakanaBalanceDisplayText`, gated the same way: only surfaces in the menu bar when there's no primary window or the user prefers the secondary metric).
- Docs: `docs/sakana.md` gets a new "Pay-as-you-go credits" section explaining the two-request shape and why; `docs/providers.md` summary/detail entries updated.

I verified this against `console.sakana.ai/billing?tab=payAsYouGo` with a live Sakana account (Standard plan) before writing the parser — captured the real rendered markup for both the credit balance card and the usage-total chart header, including the `?tab=payAsYouGo`-only server-render behavior, so the parser targets actual markup rather than guessed structure.

## Test plan
- [x] `swift build --target CodexBarCore` / `swift build --target CodexBar` — clean
- [x] `./Scripts/lint.sh format` — 0 files reformatted
- [x] `./Scripts/lint.sh lint` (swiftlint --strict) — 0 violations
- [x] `swift test --filter SakanaUsageFetcherTests` — 17/17 pass (11 existing regression tests untouched/still green + 6 new: parser present/absent/partial-data, snapshot-mapping passthrough, two-request integration test asserting both URLs hit with cookie header, best-effort-failure-doesn't-break-primary-fetch)
- [x] `make test` (full sharded suite) — green aside from a pre-existing, unrelated flaky timing assertion in `GeminiStatusProbeAPITests` (`elapsed < 3.0s` on a subprocess-kill test), which I confirmed reproduces identically on a clean `main` checkout with none of this branch's changes applied
